name: Lasagna gradient-descent flattening
method: lasagna/fit.py: staged gradient-descent fit of a flattening map, GPU only

source.note: The same commit the volume_cartographer source lock already pins, so this engine adds no second source identity to keep true.

notes.configs: Paths are resolved inside lasagna's own checkout and passed as bare positionals, which is how fit.py's cli_json.split_cfg_argv distinguishes a config from a flag. The upstream tutorial names configs/flatten_fast_nofilter.json; that file does not exist at the pinned commit, and flatten_fast.json is the nearest one that does. It leaves flatten_filter_source_angles on, which is the difference the tutorial's name refers to.
notes.device: cuda. Unlike vc_flatten this engine is not runnable on CPU in any practical time, so a CPU host is a scheduling constraint rather than a slower run.
notes.downscale: 1.0, against lasagna's own default of 4.0. The point of P3 is a sheet whose pixels still address CT voxels; downscaling throws away exactly that correspondence, the same reason the ABF++ profile sets downsample to 1.
notes.status: EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_DEFAULT because no frozen reference control has been run against this engine on this corpus. vc_flatten stays the default until one has.

non_claims: no A/B against vc_flatten has been run on this corpus; this profile exists so that comparison can be made, and records nothing about which engine is better
these are upstream's flatten_fast settings, frozen for comparability rather than tuned
a sheet this engine produces is subject to the same area-ratio floor and the same certification gate as any other; selecting it changes the flattener and nothing else
